newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bond issuance absent, eyes on rates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bond issuance absent, eyes on rates.

text.p: Issuers wary of a possible interest rate rise may unexpectedly tap the market, dealers said, despite the quiet due to lack of an official calendar for corporate bond issuance.
"We're basically hearing names as they come in," said one high-grade syndicate source. "There's still no official calendar for new issues out there."

U.S. corporations fearing higher interest rates may wish to get their financing needs met now before next Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, the policy setting arm of the Federal Reserve Board, dealers said.
Meanwhile, opportunistic issuers are expected to stand by and take advantage of any Treasury rallies to tap the market, dealers said.
"We've had a lot of issuance so far, I can't see why it would slow down with the FOMC meeting on the horizon...unless yields back up significantly," another syndicate source said.
The FOMC is scheduled to meet on Tuesday, September 24 to discuss U.S. monetary policy.
Meanwhile, on Friday no new issues have priced and only one high-yield issue is expected later in the day, syndicate sources said.
Flores & Bucks is expected to price $150 million in 10-year B3/B-minus rated subordinated notes via Merrill Lynch & Co, dealers said.
Looking ahead, Petronas is expected to price $500 million in debt via joint lead managers Salomon Brothers and CS First Boston in the next few weeks.

In Thursday's business, Philip Morris priced $650 million in five-year notes to yield a 67 basis point spread over Treasuries. The deal was upped in size from $500 million to meet investor demand, sources said.
Among new high-yield issuers were Sygnet Wireless Inc and Gray Communications Systems.
In the government market, the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond is up 1/32 at 96-11/32 to yield 7.04 percent compared with 7.04 percent at Thursday's close.
